title: fix(qa): the reference IHttpServer adapter refuses, parses or reads req.body as the IHttpRequest.body contract says
body:
Fixes #24083
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`packages/qa/http-conformance/src/adapter.ts`: the reference `NodeHttpServer` now decides `req.body` the way the standard transport decides it (`readRequestBody` in `plugin-hono-server`'s `src/request-body.ts`). Per the seat's ruling (MATCH) the decision is mirrored inside `adapter.ts` and not imported. The package keeps `@objectstack/core` as its only runtime dependency, and no export was added anywhere.

| Body sent | Reference before (`origin/main` `2bcd406a2`) | Both adapters after |
|---|---|---|
| declared JSON that does not parse (`{ not json`) | 200, `req.body` is `{}` | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`, thrown from the read |
| non-empty `text/plain` | 200, `req.body` is the string | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`, thrown from the read |
| `Text/Plain; charset=utf-8` (case) | 200, `{}` | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| empty `text/plain` | 200, `""` | 200, `{}` |
| multipart with fields | 200, `{}` | 200, the fields: last value wins, a `[]` key collects an array, a file part is a `File` |
| malformed or empty multipart | 200, `{}` | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| urlencoded `a=1&a=2&b[]=3&b[]=4` | `{"a":"2","b[]":"4"}` | `{"a":"2","b[]":["3","4"]}` |
| handler catches the refusal, answers 500 | (no refusal) | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`: the refusal replaces the handler's answer |
| a fallback (`setFallbackHandler`) reads a refused body, then throws, answers its own, or writes nothing | 500 `Fallback handler failed`, its own answer, or the 404/405 | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` on all three (patch round 1) |
| `rawBody()` on a body `req.body` refuses | the bytes | the bytes (unchanged) |

I measured all 17 request shapes with one probe that drives both adapters over a real socket, and, in patch round 1, 12 fallback shapes with a second probe. After the change, every shape answers the same status and the same body bytes on both. The one difference is the `charset=utf-8` parameter on the reference's JSON `Content-Type`. Every reference JSON answer already carried it before this change.

How it works:
- **The decision.** One module-private `readRequestBody` copies the standard transport's arms and its four refusal messages word for word.
  - Declared JSON (matched case-insensitively): empty or whitespace is `{}`, anything else that does not parse is refused.
  - A form, `multipart/form-data` or `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, is parsed by Node's own Fetch `Response.formData()`. This is the parser hono's `bufferToFormData` calls. The field shape follows hono 4.13.12's `convertFormDataToBodyData` with `all: false, dot: false`, and its null prototype too.
  - For any other media type nothing is read. The body is refused on read when the framing headers declare one (RFC 9112 §6.3), and is `{}` otherwise.
  - GET and HEAD read no bytes from the socket, as `@hono/node-server` hands them a request with no body.
- **`req.body` is an accessor** with a setter, as on the standard transport. A route that reads only `rawBody()` never meets the refusal. `rawBody()` now caches the read as one promise, so a body the decision already consumed hands back the same bytes, or the same read failure.
- **The answer side** (mechanism assumption 1, measured below). On a matched route and in the fallback alike, once a read of `req.body` meets the refusal, anything the handler writes after it is dropped. `writeBodyRefusal` then answers `400 {"success":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":...}}`, the two keys the standard transport's `declaredEnvelopeForThrow` renders for this throw. In the fallback branch (patch round 1, seat ruling `6244250024`) it answers on every arm: the fallback threw, caught and answered, or caught and wrote nothing. This is what the standard transport's fallback answers, because it runs through the same `runHandler` as its routes. Untouched: the generic catch arm, which reads `statusCode` only and answers an `{error}` body (`adapter.test.ts`'s `maps thrown errors with statusCode` pins it), and the fallback's `500 Fallback handler failed` for a throw that read no refused body (`fallback-seam.conformance.test.ts` G5-a pins it). Guarantee 4's docblock now names the one exception: a fallback that read a refused body.

New `packages/qa/http-conformance/src/request-body.conformance.test.ts`. Its route handlers read `req.body` and run on BOTH adapters over a real socket. Per adapter, it covers:
- malformed declared JSON;
- non-empty `text/plain`;
- multipart fields: single, repeated, `[]`, a file part;
- a handler that catches the refusal and writes its own answer;
- `rawBody()` of a refused body;
- the controls: no body, an empty JSON body and an empty `text/plain` body are each `{}`, and valid JSON is the document.
- the fallback (patch round 1): a fallback that reads a refused body and then throws, catches and answers, or catches and writes nothing is answered with the refusal. Its controls: a fallback that never reads the body and writes nothing leaves the 404, and the 405 + `Allow`; one that reads a valid JSON body gets the document.

A parity block then sends each of 16 rows to both adapters and asserts the same status and the same bytes, refusal messages included. A change to either side's wording therefore reds here.

`packages/qa/http-conformance/README.md` (patch round 1): the one line that listed multipart parsing as deliberately absent now says what the adapter does. JSON and forms (multipart included) are parsed into `req.body`, and every other media type stays raw behind the lazy `req.rawBody()`.

## PM mechanism assumptions, measured

1. **Partly falsified.**
   - Held: the standard transport refuses from the `body` read, not before the handler, and a route that reads only `rawBody()` is unaffected.
   - Did not hold: its answer does not take "the same declared-error path every thrown declared error takes". `runHandler` has a dedicated `refusedBodyRead` arm that answers the refusal whatever the handler made of the throw, a caught throw included (probe: a handler that caught it and wrote 500 still answered 400). Only the renderer, `declaredEnvelopeForThrow`, is shared.
   - The reference did not render a declared throw at all. A route throwing `{ status: 400, code: 'INVALID_REQUEST' }` answered `500 {"error":"declared refusal"}`. So the answer-side change above was required. It is the smallest change that reproduces the replacement, and it does not touch the generic catch arm.
2. **Held.** The standard transport parses both form types through `parseBody()`. Node's built-in `Response.formData()` matches every field shape the case reaches without a dependency: a single value, a repeated key (last wins), a `[]` key (array) and a file part (`File`).
3. **Held.** `rawBody()` reads the bytes of every body, refused ones included. The suite pins it for malformed JSON and `text/plain`. Multipart `rawBody()` is the held-off hono cache question and is not asserted.
4. **Held.** No existing assert pinned an old answer, so `adapter.test.ts` is unchanged. `fallback-seam.conformance.test.ts` is unchanged too: its only 500 assert, G5-a, is a fallback that throws its own error on a body-less GET and never reads a refused body. These suites drive the reference and read `body`, and all pass on `6544c545a`:
   - `adapter.test.ts` (16)
   - `fallback-seam.conformance.test.ts` (18)
   - `conformance.integration.test.ts` (30)
   - `query-multiplicity.conformance.test.ts` (8)
   - `response-observation.conformance.test.ts` (14)

## Ablation (once, the card's acceptance 3)

`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (WRAP mode, with an `EXIT INT TERM` trap) restored the old arm `let body: any = {}; try { body = text ? JSON.parse(text) : {}; } catch { body = {}; }` in place of the malformed-JSON refusal. No build is involved: the suite imports `./adapter.js` from source.

- The mutation landed on disk: anchor 1 to 0, old arm 0 to 1, blob `8204c4fa1a35` to `9b952dea3e0e`.
- **Red:** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/http-conformance exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/request-body.conformance.test.ts`, verify-lock `VERDICT command-exit 1`, `Tests 2 failed | 22 passed (24)`. The two failures:
  - `... on the 'node' adapter > a malformed declared-JSON body is refused 400 INVALID_REQUEST at the read, never read as {}`
  - the parity row `/echo · malformedJson`
- Every `hono` leg stayed green. The parity row is cross-adapter by construction, so it reds whenever the reference drifts.
- **Restore** proved: blob equals HEAD (`8204c4fa1a35`), and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- **Green:** same command on `9e5b8b1e2`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`, `Tests 24 passed (24)`.

Patch round 1, once: `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs --delete` (WRAP mode, with an `EXIT INT TERM` trap) removed the fallback branch's one refusal-answer line, `if (refusedBodyRead) return this.writeBodyRefusal(nodeRes, refusedBodyRead);`.
- The mutation landed on disk: line count 1 to 0, blob `d3cdbc3cfd7a` to `54509553a9f2`.
- **Red:** the same vitest command, `VERDICT command-exit 1`, `Tests 6 failed | 34 passed (40)`. The six failures:
  - the three `node` fallback legs: the refused-read-then-throw leg answered `500 Fallback handler failed`, and the caught-and-answered and caught-and-silent legs answered `404 ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND`;
  - their three parity rows: `/fallback/throw`, `/fallback/caught-answers`, `/fallback/caught-silent`.
- Every `hono` leg stayed green, and so did both fallback controls.
- **Restore** proved: blob equals HEAD (`d3cdbc3cfd7a`), and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- **Green:** the whole suite on `6544c545a`, `Tests 190 passed (190)`, with `request-body.conformance.test.ts` at 40 of 40.

## Tests (final head `6544c545a`, after merging `origin/main` `7be3cc728`)

- First rebuilt the closure under the verify lock: `pnpm turbo run build --filter='@objectstack/http-conformance^...' --concurrency=2`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`, 36/36 tasks.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/http-conformance exec vitest run --reporter=verbose`: exit 0, `Test Files 15 passed (15)`, `Tests 190 passed (190)`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/http-conformance typecheck`: exit 0. This and the line above ran joined by `&&` under one `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
  - `tsc --noEmit` passes, and so does `check:test-typecheck`: 3 files / 27 errors / 10 signatures held, unchanged.
  - The new test file carries no ledger entry, so it compiles with zero errors.
- `test:repo`, each exit captured on its own, all 0 (re-run in patch round 1, spec included, since its repo tests walk `packages/**`):

  | Package | Files | Tests |
  |---|---|---|
  | `@objectstack/core` | 6 | 86 |
  | `@objectstack/objectql` | 1 | 5 |
  | `@objectstack/rest` | 5 | 262 passed, 14 skipped |
  | `@objectstack/runtime` | 3 | 808 |
  | `@objectstack/types` | 1 | 11 |
  | `@objectstack/spec` | 67 | 1115 |

## Gates (final head `6544c545a`)

- `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config` on both changed `.ts` files: exit 0, no output.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived the same 52 commands as round 0. 51 exited 0.
- `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3 (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET`): it reads every package's `dist/`, and only this package's closure is built locally. NOT MEASURED locally; CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` runs it and is green on `6544c545a`.
- `dispatch-gates --ran`: `52 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 51 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED (1 DERIVED from a recorded exit 3)`.
- Clause-② judged from this diff:
  - `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` has no CLI. Run bare it prints nothing and exits 0. Its `readClause2Line` export reads this body's line as `{"kind":"declared","value":"no","arm":null}`.
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main --event` (this body) on the final diff: exit 0, its `LEVEL AXIS` line for a declared clause-② `no`, with no direction arm. No narrowing face was read.

## Changeset

None. `@objectstack/http-conformance` is `"private": true` and publishes nothing, which is the repo's private-package fast lane for `skip-changeset`. The package's `CHANGELOG.md` has only ever carried dependency bumps, and the precedent test-only change `6a53564b9` shipped without one. The `skip-changeset` label is applied after this PR is created.

## Acceptance notes

- **README line (fixed in patch round 1).** The README line that listed multipart parsing as deliberately absent is corrected in this PR, per seat ruling `6244250024`.
- **Fallback seam (fixed in patch round 1).** A fallback that reads a refused body is now answered with the refusal on the reference too, on every arm, as on the standard transport. Seat ruling `6244250024` lifted the hold-off for the answer path only.
- **Fallback contract wording (spec, held off).** In `packages/spec/src/contracts/http-server.ts`, the `setFallbackHandler` sentence "A handler that writes no response leaves the adapter's standard unmatched-request answer in place" names no exception. Both adapters now answer a fallback that read a refused body and wrote nothing with `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, as the `IHttpRequest.body` paragraph says the standard transport does. The wording is the spec lane's; nothing here edits it.
- **Handler writes before it reads.** A handler that WROTE before it read a refused body cannot be replaced on `node:http`: its bytes are already on the wire. The standard transport buffers the answer and still replaces it. The code documents this; no conformance case reaches it.
- **Middleware reads `req.body`.** `use()` middleware on the reference receives the real request, so a middleware that reads `req.body` meets the refusal. The standard transport hands middleware an empty request. The middleware contract does not populate `body`, and no case reaches it.
- **Content-Type charset.** The reference's JSON answers carry `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`, and the standard transport's carry `application/json`. This predates the change and covers every reference JSON answer.
- **Hono multipart `rawBody()` cache.** The hold-off named by the card is not touched or asserted here.
